estimate.damage_summary: An atmospheric overvoltage event damaged the television and speaker system connected to the building electrical installation. A technician subsequently attended to confirm the surge failure and check the wiring.
estimate.policy_notes: The electronics are covered under clauses 2.3.3 and 4.2.4, subject to the EUR 5,000 gross appliance sub-limit and the standard-grade replacement basis in clauses 7.1.1 and 7.1.9. Because the description establishes that no surge-protective device was used, clause 2.3.3 halves the otherwise payable amount for each affected appliance. Contractor diagnostics and reports are not repair costs under clause 7.1.8(e); a call-out charge is payable only alongside indemnifiable work on the same invoice under clause 7.1.8(d).

lines.invoice_text: Surge-damaged home electronics (speaker system and TV set)
lines.rationale: Clauses 2.3.3 and 4.2.4 cover the two appliances because physical surge damage is described and shown, while clauses 7.1.1 and 7.1.9 limit replacement to equivalent standard-grade items. The stated absence of a surge-protective device triggers the 50% reduction in clause 2.3.3; two units are plausible, but the unspecified models leave the reasonable replacement price uncertain.

lines.invoice_text: Diagnostic surge-failure report and technician call-out
lines.rationale: Although the attendance relates to the reported surge, the diagnostic report is the contractor’s own diagnostic work and is excluded as a repair cost by clause 7.1.8(e). Under clause 7.1.8(d), the call-out is not payable on an invoice without indemnifiable work; one attendance at most is plausible for the described visit, rather than three.
